# Writing a document an agent reads

- **A pointer document holds pointers, not detail.** `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` load in full every session, so detail belongs in a path-scoped rule or a skill, referenced from there.
- **Put the rule where the agent will be when it needs it.** A standard that applies to `.cs` files belongs in a path-scoped rule, not in a skill that has to be judged relevant first.
- **Never put a rule behind a link alone.** Some readers — Copilot code review among them — cannot follow one. State the rule, then link for depth.
- **Be specific enough to verify.** "Use 2-space indentation" over "format properly"; "run `pnpm test` before committing" over "test your changes". A vague instruction is followed vaguely.
- **Do not contradict a sibling document.** Where two rules disagree, an agent picks one arbitrarily — which is worse than either alone. If you are adding a rule that overlaps an existing one, change the existing one instead.
- **A standard that applies beyond this repository belongs upstream**, in the shared packs, not copied into a second place where it can drift.

# Editing a skill or a rule

- `name` in frontmatter matches the directory name.
- **A description change is a behaviour change.** It is the triggering logic and it sits permanently in context, so it needs an activation case in both directions — what must fire, and which sibling must stay silent.
- Keep a rules file short. It loads on every matching edit; if it runs past a screen, most of it belongs in the skill.
- **Attribute adapted work in the file itself**, naming the source and its licence. These files are redistributed, so a notice in a parent document does not travel. Never strip an attribution footer to tidy a file up.
